Butyl 4-ami- nobenzoate. C11H15NO2 = 193.2. CAS — 94-25-7. Pharmacopoeias. In Fr. and US. USP 31 (Butamben). A white, odourless, crystalline powder. M.p. 57° to 59°. Soluble 1 in 7000 of water; soluble in alcohol, in ether, in chloroform, in fixed oils, and in dilute acids. It slowly hydrolyses when boiled with water. Butyl Aminobenzoate Picrate Abbott-34842; Butamben Picrate (USAN); Butilaminobenzoato, picrato de. (C11H15NO2)2,C6H3N3O7 = 615.6. CAS — 577-48-0. Profile Butyl aminobenzoate, a para-aminobenzoic acid ester, is a local anaesthetic (p.1850) that has been used for surface anaesthesia of the skin and mucous membranes. It has also been used for relief of pain and pruritus associated with anorectal disorders. A sus- pension of butyl aminobenzoate 5 or 10% has been given epidur- ally. Butyl aminobenzoate picrate has been applied to the skin as an ointment. ◊ References. 1. Korsten HH, et al.
